claims.value: Opened May 1872; construction 1870–1872; timber (mataī) Gothic Revival

source.source_name: Heritage New Zealand List No. 294

claims.note: The building was designed by W. F. Crisp, and Frederick Strouts supervised from 1871. Christchurch City Libraries calls the present church 'the third on the site' and says it was 'consecrated in 1872'.

status_assessment.basis: On 2026-09-10 the parish website lists regular Sunday and weekday Masses and a Sunday Evensong. It also carries news items dated 3 and 10 September 2026 announcing upcoming Sunday services, and a Michaelmas High Mass on 29 September. The diocesan Anglican Life directory says Mass is celebrated every day. I found no evidence of closure, sale or deconsecration in any source consulted. The building survived the 2010–2011 earthquakes and stayed in use.
status_assessment.osm_stale_basis: OSM version 12 (2024-10-13) matches the sources on the substantive points: an active Anglican Christian place of worship at 84 Oxford Terrace, building dated 1872, Heritage NZ list 294. Two details are outdated or imprecise but do not change the description of the site. The website tag (chchstmichaels.org.nz) no longer resolves; the parish now uses stmichaelandallangels.nz. And start_date=1872 records the building date, whereas worship on the site began in 1851.

run_manifest.notes: claude session 80c4c9e0-28d4-4527-937d-f36b0d8fcd07; num_turns 18; permission_denials 0 | A quoted_support passage joined with '...' links fragments from the same page. The fetch tool returned extracted text, not raw HTML, so every quotation should be checked against the live page. Two points need a reviewer. First, the address: Heritage NZ, Wikipedia, OSM and LINZ give 84 Oxford Terrace, while the parish website and Anglican Life give 86-90 Oxford Terrace. Second, the OSM start_date=1872 is the building date, not the start of worship (1851). One early fetch summary of the Heritage NZ page called the church a 'stone structure'. That was an error in the summary: Heritage NZ's own text says it is timber (mataī), and the church stands on rubble stone foundations. The Wikipedia summary also names the current vicar; this is left out under the living-persons rule. OSM editor usernames are left out for the same reason. The Papers Past search page came back empty through the fetch tool, so the 1851 and 1872 dates have no contemporary newspaper support yet; they rest on Heritage NZ, Wikipedia and Christchurch City Libraries. The organ damage (2011) and reinstatement (2013) appear only in the Wikipedia summary, without a verbatim quote, so they are not recorded as claims. The separate belfry listing (Heritage NZ No. 295) was not opened.
